title: Contractual frictions and the patterns of trade: the role of generalized trust
publisher: Journal of International Trade & Economic Development 29(7), 775–796
summary: The paper looks at informal contracting institutions, measured by generalised trust, as a source of comparative advantage. Countries with higher trust export relatively more in industries prone to contractual frictions, which may explain why countries with weak formal institutions can still hold a cost advantage in contract-intensive industries.
keyFindings: Higher-trust countries export relatively more in industries prone to contractual frictions.
Higher-trust countries enter more export markets and ship more products to each destination.
